It started out innocently enough. In fact it was hailed as perhaps the greatest invention in mankinds history. For the first time people were able to control and remember their dreams. The myWorld device gave users a whole new and separate life. A means of escape. A hope for the future. Many mental ailments were cured or alleviated as each night users plugged themselves in and lived out their fantasies.

Then came the recording abilities. We shared our dreams with one another, and this too was hailed as a great leap for mankind. Real life pornography and prostitution became a relic of the past. Crime dropped. Drug use dropped. Psychiatric fields flourished, and our study of the human brain reached new heights. The most common videos shared were of people having sex with coworkers or acquaintances they had met passively on the street. But even from the beginning it was the really sick shit that went viral.

The invention was so life-changing and great that we justified anything and everything we saw with "it's not real". It wasn't really a man murdering his boss and raping his wife and daughter, it was just some sicko's fantasies. It wasn't really child pornography, as there was no real child. It wasn't really someone murdering the president. Hitler wasn't really alive. That man wasn't really wearing a suit made of human flesh. The world wasn't really destroyed in a nuclear holocaust. No one really found a way to kill all the white people. No one was actually hurt, we said. Perhaps we were right.

But the debate became intense. The myWorld device was outlawed in many countries, but the huge demand created thriving black markets. Even as we fiercely debated the newfound implications of such technology, the debate was growing less relevant by the day as the technology became less expensive and spread throughout the world. One thing became clear to everyone - there was no going back.

Then came the "ad supported" version for the myWorld device. You could get a free device, and the only difference was in your dream you might have the sudden urge to drink a brand of soda you'd never tried before, or your dream car might have a few more "Chevy" decals. It was free so why not give it a try?

But the implications of thought-insertion turned out to be farther reaching than almost anyone had imagined...
